zh: 鸟每次都回到固定的鸟巢再出发，所以每一侧被取走的顺序就是这一侧木棒从近到远的顺序，与另一侧无关。
预先列出巢右侧的木棒下标（按下标递增）和左侧的木棒下标（按下标递减），然后右、左交替从两个列表依次取下一项，直到累计长度 ≥100。
建 right、left 两个列表；第 k 次（从 0 开始）偶数取 right[k/2]、奇数取 left[k/2]，记录下标并累加长度，累计 ≥100 立即停止；按采集顺序用空格输出原始下标。注意不能按长度或全局距离排序。
en: The bird always returns to the fixed nest before setting out again, so the order in which one side's sticks are taken is simply that side's sticks from nearest to farthest, independent of the other side.

List the stick indices to the right of the nest (increasing index) and to the left (decreasing index) in advance, then take the next item alternately from the right list and the left list until the total length reaches 100.

Build the lists right and left; on pick k (from 0), take right[k/2] when k is even and left[k/2] when k is odd, record the index and add its length, and stop as soon as the total is ≥ 100; print the original indices in collection order separated by spaces. Do not sort by length or by overall distance.

explanationEn:
## Fixing the original OCR and corrections to the curated page

Files OA LIST/Visa_OA/004_QQ_1741880069560.txt through 007_QQ_1741880100789.txt in fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc give the full rules. After each stick is taken the bird returns to the initial position bird, then searches in the opposite direction for the nearest stick; the first search goes right. It stops as soon as the cumulative stick length is at least 100, and returns the original 0-based indices in collection order.

File 007 specifies 3≤forest.length≤1000, 0≤forest[i]≤50, 0≤bird<forest.length. File 004 guarantees forest[bird]=0 and sum(forest)≥100. Files 004-005 further guarantee explicitly that throughout the process, whenever the bird needs to go right there is still a non-zero stick on the right, and whenever it needs to go left there is still one on the left; it never goes out of bounds because the required direction runs empty before reaching 100. This guarantee is stronger than the total being at least 100. The site keeps it in full and invents no rule for switching direction or stopping when sticks run out; the generator screens inputs with an independent simulation, and inputs violating the guarantee do not enter judging.

The company MDX omits the return to the initial position, and its code continues searching from the last collection position; its example also sets forest[bird]=3 and contains 80, violating the original empty nest and the upper bound of 50. The site restores the OCR and does not reuse that invalid example. The original example is [25,0,50,0,0,0,0,15,0,0,45] with bird=4: positions 7, 2, 10 are taken in turn, with running totals 15, 65, 110, and the output is [7,2,10]. The site serializes the returned array as one line of space-separated indices; the two other public examples are both explicitly marked as site-added. No upstream code was executed.

## Approach

List all stick indices to the left of the nest in decreasing index order, and those to the right in increasing order. Each list is then the collection order from the nest outward, nearest first. Alternately take the next item from the right list and the left list, add its length to the total, and stop once the total reaches 100. Even when two sticks have the same length they are collected by position; do not sort by length or by global distance.

## Proof of correctness

The bird always returns to the fixed nest. Consider either side: taken sticks become empty, while the other sticks stay where they were. So the next time the bird sets out toward that side, it finds exactly the first stick not yet taken in that side's nearest-to-farthest list. By induction, the left and right lists exactly represent the collection order on each side.

The source rule starts on the right and switches direction after every collection. The reference program alternates between the right and left lists by the parity of the answer length, and reads the next index according to how many times that side has been visited, so the stick chosen at every step is the same as in the original process. The running total is the same at every step too, and controlling the loop with total<100 makes the stopping moment the same. The original problem guarantees that the required side has a stick whenever the threshold has not yet been reached, so every read is valid. Hence the output index sequence is exactly correct.

## Complexity and boundaries

Building the two index lists takes O(n), and each stick is taken at most once, for O(n) total time and O(n) space. Every positive length is at least 1, so at most 100 sticks are taken; before stopping the total is ≤99 and the last stick is ≤50, so the final total is ≤149. Hitting exactly 100 and exceeding 100 must both stop immediately. When n=3, a valid array must have 50 on each side of the empty nest; n=1000, sparse sides, long runs of 0 and sticks all of length 1 are all handled directly.

## Independent verification

163 unique oracles each walk cell by cell from the fixed bird position, set the first non-zero value to 0 and take it, then return to the origin and reverse direction; they build no left/right lists and do not call the reference program. All oracle and official inputs are checked against the full source ranges and the per-round stick guarantee. In addition, for n=3..7 with values in 0/25/50, all empty-nest positions were enumerated: 2590 valid inputs were compared one by one against the reference, and 3412 inputs whose total is sufficient but which lack a stick in some round were independently identified and excluded; only statistics and a summary are recorded, and they are not used for judging.

The official cases cover the original example, exact 100 and overshoot, 100 consecutive sticks of length 1, sparse sides, n=1000, the maximum value 50, extreme valid nest positions, and layouts where distance and length point in opposite directions. Two kinds of wrong programs reproduce, respectively, the MDX post-collection position shift (first stepping one cell in the old direction and then searching in reverse, which can wrongly take the next stick on the same side), and continuing after reaching exactly 100; each is counted as killed only after it exits normally on all official data. Merely searching cell by cell in reverse from the last stick can itself be equivalent to returning to the nest, so such an equivalent implementation must not be counted as a negative control.
